name: Transient Predisposition to Invasive Pyogenic Bacterial Infection
aliases: Temporary Susceptibility to Invasive Bacterial Infection

criteria.description: History of recurrent invasive pyogenic bacterial infections within a defined transient period
Exclusion of chronic or permanent immunodeficiency disorders by immunological testing
Demonstrated resolution of infection susceptibility after transient period without ongoing immunodeficiency
Laboratory evidence of transient neutropenia or impaired neutrophil function during infection episodes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: recurrent invasive infections, exclusion of chronic immunodeficiency, and documented resolution of susceptibility.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of permanent immunodeficiencies and confirmation of transient nature.

laboratory: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)
Normal immunoglobulin levels excluding chronic immunodeficiency
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing localized abscesses
other: Resolution of susceptibility without long-term immunodeficiency

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations in NADPH oxidase complex
Chronic rather than transient infection susceptibility
Early onset with failure to thrive
Broad susceptibility to viral, bacterial, and fungal infections

redFlags: Recurrent invasive bacterial infections beyond infancy
Failure to resolve infection susceptibility after expected transient period
Signs of systemic sepsis or septic shock
references: Orphanet: Transient Predisposition to Invasive Pyogenic Bacterial Infection, ORPHA:70592
